text:
Executive Summary

This Place Delivery Agreement (PDA) is dated 30 October 2026. It will strengthen the relationship between the East Midlands Combined County Authority (EMCCA), Homes England (the trading name for the Homes and Communities Agency), and the National Housing Bank (NHB). It provides an enhanced single delivery framework to accelerate housing delivery, unlock regeneration and underpin EMCCA’s Vision for Growth to transform productivity across the region.

Building on the success of the existing Strategic Place Partnership (SPP), this Agreement represents a step change in the way the 3 organisations work together. It moves beyond collaboration towards co-delivery, bringing together local leadership, national expertise and investment capability behind a shared set of priorities.

This Agreement represents an enhanced model of place-based delivery. By combining local leadership, devolved influence, dedicated delivery capability, aligned investment and stronger accountability, EMCCA, Homes England and the NHB will work together to deliver more homes, unlock regeneration, attract investment and drive long-term economic growth across the region.

Through this Agreement, the partners commit to:

Delivering strategic growth and regeneration priorities

Supporting EMCCA’s most significant housing, regeneration and growth opportunities.

Enabling housing investment closer to place

Aligning investment decisions with regional priorities and strengthening EMCCA’s influence over housing delivery.

Accelerating affordable and social housing delivery

Supporting the delivery of social, affordable and council housing through aligned funding and delivery support.

Unlocking investment and delivery capability at scale

Mobilising public and private capital while strengthening the region’s ability to deliver complex projects.

Establishing a Joint Delivery Unit (JDU)

Creating a single delivery structure bringing together EMCCA, Homes England and NHB expertise, investment and delivery capability, under nominated Co-Directors from EMCCA and Homes England.

Strengthening accountability and governance

Providing clear routes for decision-making and escalation, ensuring barriers to delivery can be addressed rapidly and jointly by EMCCA, Homes England and NHB, with day-to-day responsibility for the delivery of the Agreement being held by the Homes England Executive Director for the Midlands.

Commencement and term

This PDA shall commence on the date hereof and shall continue for an initial period of 3 years (subject to an annual review) and shall thereafter continue for such further period or periods as shall be agreed in writing between the parties, provided always that any party may give not less than 90 days prior written notice to the others to terminate this PDA at any time.

1. Strategic context: East Midlands Combined County Authority’s growth ambitions

Place overview

1.1 The East Midlands is a region of scale, character and opportunity comprising 2 historic counties, 2 dynamic cities, a network of industrious towns, and nationally significant rural areas.

1.2 Home to nearly 2.3 million people and an economic output of £60 billion (GVA), the region is well connected at the heart of the country with key strengths in advanced manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences, the visitor economy, and a fast-growing digital, creative and cultural sector.

East Midlands Combined County Authority area map

The map shows the East Midlands Combined County Authority area, covering Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Derby and Nottingham, and its location within the UK.

This diagram could not be made accessible. 1.3 EMCCA brings together the local authorities of Derby City, Derbyshire, Nottingham City and Nottinghamshire. EMCCA works in partnership with constituent authorities and stakeholders to develop and deliver policies, programmes and services that directly benefit the people of the East Midlands.

Housing and growth ambitions

1.4 In October 2025, EMCCA launched the East Midlands Vision for Growth. This is a long-term economic strategy, led by Mayor Claire Ward, to create 100,000 new jobs, build up to 100,000 homes, and add billions to the regional economy. The vision recognises that opportunities and challenges cross local boundaries. By working through EMCCA, the region can take a more strategic approach, plan at scale, attract investment and deliver better outcomes.

1.5 Underpinning this vision will be the region’s first Spatial Development Strategy and new Housing Strategy. These will set out the Mayor’s ambition to not only deliver more homes, but to deliver the right mix of housing in the right places, while also improving the quality of existing housing stock. Specifically, the Mayor’s ambition is that by 2040 the housing affordability gap in the East Midlands will be closing, with rents and house prices better aligned to local incomes; and communities will have access to safe and warm housing, suitable to their needs, enabling people to live healthy lives in connected communities.

1.6 The Mayor’s ambition is for new homes to be delivered on brownfield sites and for delivery to support town centre and high street regeneration. New homes will need to address the challenges set out here and be both affordable and meet local tenure requirements.

Housing and regeneration challenges

1.7 The East Midlands has a strong track record of housing delivery, with 33,049 homes delivered over the last 3 years, 32% above government housing delivery targets. All areas within the EMCCA region are meeting their National Planning Policy Framework targets. However, districts like Derbyshire Dales and Erewash require a 160% increase in housing production to meet their new targets.

1.8 Despite this strong track record, affordable housing supply has not kept pace with demand. Over the last 17 years, social housing stock has increased by just 1.5%, while England’s total social housing stock in that period increased by 6.4%. While 2,318 affordable homes were completed in 2025, the net increase after Right to Buy losses was only 920 homes.

1.9 Homes are gradually becoming more affordable across the region, with the average affordability ratio for Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire falling consecutively over the last few years, from 7.43 in 2023, to 6.93 in 2024, and 6.66 in 2025. This improvement has largely been driven by wage growth alongside stable house prices. However, affordability pressures vary significantly across the region. Rural districts such as Rushcliffe (9.15) and Derbyshire Dales (8.94) remain the least affordable areas, while former industrial areas such as Bolsover (4.98) and Chesterfield (5.23) are considerably more affordable. Around Nottingham, affordability pressures are increasingly concentrated in surrounding commuter authorities rather than the city itself, while Mansfield and Ashfield remain among the region’s most affordable housing markets. Derby presents a different pattern, with the city being more affordable than its commuter areas. These variations will have significant implications for affordable and social housing provision in the region, requiring distinct place-based responses across urban, suburban, market towns and rural areas.

1.10 Homelessness is a particular challenge for the region. During financial year 2025 and 2026, local authorities across EMCCA assessed 10,492 households as homeless or threatened with homelessness and owed them a prevention or relief duty under the Homelessness Reduction Act. This equates to around 874 households each month, or 29 households every day, being assessed as homeless or at risk of homelessness and requiring statutory support.

Barriers to delivery

1.11 There are a range of barriers to delivery that the JDU will work together to address. These include:

Infrastructure gaps

Achieving EMCCA’s growth ambitions will require substantial investment in transport connectivity, enabling works for major housing and employment sites, digital connectivity, and the social infrastructure needed to support growing communities.

Viability challenges

There are significant viability challenges across the region impacting development. This particularly impacts SME developers.

Planning delays

Local Planning Authorities face significant capacity challenges which are slowing down planning approvals. This is also being impacted by capacity in statutory and non-statutory consultees.

Construction skills

The construction sector is facing a severe skills shortage, stalling essential housing and infrastructure projects.

2. Going further, faster, and rewiring the state

2.1 The SPP agreed in December 2025 cemented ongoing collaboration between EMCCA and Homes England around thematic and delivery priorities.

The SPP identified 3 strategic priorities, which continue to guide the activities and operation of the partnership and JDU.

Priority 1 — Improve the supply of high quality, energy efficient homes and additional affordable homes providing greater choice and opportunity for more people to access a home in the EMCCA region that meets their needs.

Priority 2 — Develop and maintain a robust pipeline of investable propositions that unlock housing delivery and regeneration in the East Midlands — supporting the region’s ambitions for economic growth, sustainability, placemaking and reuse of brownfield sites.

Priority 3 — Adopt a place-based approach and align resources with key priorities alongside important national and local partners.

2.2 There is now an opportunity to go further and faster towards a model of place-based co-delivery designed to better meet the needs of the region. EMCCA, Homes England, and the NHB will combine local leadership, national expertise, and investment capability through a dedicated JDU, aligned investment activity, and shared accountability for outcomes.

2.3 This approach will accelerate housing delivery, unlock regeneration opportunities and support sustainable economic growth across the region. The JDU, operating under the strategic leadership of the Mayor and EMCCA, will provide a single delivery framework which brings together land, funding, specialist technical expertise, investment capability and powers, through which strategic ambition can be translated into investable propositions, faster decision-making and tangible delivery outcomes.

Place Delivery Agreement: A new strategic framework to serve places and local leaders

2.4 The PDA establishes a single framework through which EMCCA, Homes England, and the NHB will align resources, expertise, capacity, investment and delivery activity. It is intended to retain sufficient flexibility to respond to changing circumstances and emerging priorities.

2.5 The Agreement focuses on a small number of strategic priorities where a coordinated approach can have the greatest impact in overcoming barriers to delivery, attracting investment and bringing forward transformational housing and regeneration outcomes. More broadly, partners will maintain and enhance the existing Regional Housing Pipeline which will guide the deployment of resources, specialist support and investment activity.

2.6 This framework is intended to ensure that regional priorities, national and local capability, and land, investment, powers and expertise are aligned around a common set of delivery objectives.

3. Theme A: Spatial priorities

3.1 The Vision for Growth identifies 6 strategic locations to supercharge the region. These include: the Trent Arc, Canal Corridor, Supercluster, the Peaks and Dales, Heartlands, and Derwent Valley Mills.

3.2 Alongside supporting transformational growth and regeneration opportunities, accelerating the delivery of social and affordable housing is a strategic priority for this partnership. EMCCA, Homes England, and the NHB will work together to maximise the impact of the Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) and support delivery across the region.

3.3 A core purpose of this PDA is to provide the Mayor and local leaders across the East Midlands with the tools they need to deliver their most ambitious housing, regeneration and growth priorities. Achieving transformational change will require dedicated delivery capability, coordinated investment and long-term partnership.

3.4 The priorities here represent the initial focus of activity under the PDA and will be reviewed periodically to ensure resources remain focused on the opportunities where joint intervention can deliver the greatest strategic impact.

Strategic place priority 1: Trent Arc

3.5 The most significant opportunities lie in the Trent Arc — the area including and between the cities of Derby and Nottingham. This includes transformational city centre projects and major housing growth, complemented by investment in transport and economic growth.

The Trent Arc has the potential to deliver:

30,000 new homes

more than 40,000 full-time jobs

a £2.4 billion boost to the economy

2.7 million square metres of commercial space

3.6 The scale, complexity and strategic importance of the opportunity requires a coordinated approach to support the establishment of the coherent long-term regeneration programme capable of unlocking growth at scale.

3.7 Significant progress is already being made in developing and delivering key projects across the Trent Arc which will remain priorities for delivery by the JDU. These include:

Nottingham city centre

3.8 As in many city centres, changing economic trends in Nottingham have resulted in opportunities for transformational change and housing growth. Building on successful partnership working to date between HE, EMCCA and Nottingham City Council. The progression of key projects such as Broad Marsh in Nottingham city centre will be priorities for the JDU. At Broad Marsh the demolition of obsolete buildings and the procurement of a development partner is underway to enable the delivery of around 1,000 new homes, 20,000 square metres of retail, office, and community space, and up to 2,000 full-time jobs in the heart of the city centre.

Fairham

3.9 Fairham is a 3,000-home sustainable urban extension being delivered by Homes England and partner landowners. Its location within the Trent Arc and its scale make it strategically important for housing delivery in the region. Progress includes outline consent for 3,000 homes and associated town centre, leisure, connectivity and green space, completion of most of the on-site highway infrastructure, plans submitted for a primary school opening in 2028, and a business park that is around 50% complete, supporting over 1,200 jobs. Through the JDU EMCCA’s convening role in the region can support the delivery of the scheme and associated transport infrastructure where appropriate.

Team Derby

3.10 Team Derby is a strategic partnership between local, regional and national government, industry and academia, focused on accelerating economic growth and regeneration across Derby. Building on the city’s strengths and ambitious plans to grow the defence, nuclear, advanced manufacturing and rail sectors, the partnership seeks to ensure that investment delivers tangible benefits for local people through better jobs, skills, homes and places. The partnership is supported by an initial £10 million government investment in capital funding to deliver high impact projects that create visible growth. Team Derby is organised around 5 workstreams: Raising Aspirations and Skills Pathway, City Centre Offer, Homes for the Future, Investment and Economic Growth, and Infinity Park.

3.11 The Homes for the Future workstream brings together partners from Homes England, EMCCA, Derby City Council, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) and the private sector to support Derby’s long-term growth ambitions. HE’s role is to convene and align partners around a shared agenda, enabling collaborative action to unlock housing delivery and investment opportunities. The workstream is focused on developing an approach to increasing affordable housing supply in the city, bringing forward investable housing propositions, unlocking stalled housing sites, and ensuring housing delivery supports Derby’s economic growth ambitions. A key objective is to ensure the city has the homes required to accommodate both existing residents and the future workforce attracted by major investments such as Infinity Park.

Derby city centre (including Station Quarter)

3.12 The growth of Derby city centre offers opportunities to deliver around 5,500 new homes, alongside retail led regeneration. The area around the train station is central to this ambition but faces challenges including poor-quality land uses, large surface car parks, fragmented ownership, and poor connectivity.

3.13 The Station Quarter project will deliver major residential led mixed-use regeneration around the station including up to 1,500 new homes, a new station square, high-quality public realm, a mobility hub, improved active travel infrastructure and rationalised parking. The first phase will deliver 597 new homes and 3,490 square metres of retail and, or, office space. Along with organisational expertise, Homes England is providing significant revenue funding for this project. EMCCA has committed £3.5 million for acquisitions. This activity will continue to be a priority for the JDU.

South Derbyshire Growth Zone and Infinity Garden Village

3.14 Infinity Garden Village (IGV) is a well-designed housing-led sustainable extension that is part of South Derbyshire Growth Zone encompassing the southern extension of Infinity Park Derby, a major hub for advanced manufacturing, logistics, and innovation, and one of the government’s Investment Zones. It is identified as a flagship development within EMCCA’s Trent Arc Spatial Growth Strategy, hosting Rolls-Royce’s Nuclear Skills Academy and located adjacent to Rolls-Royce’s global civil aerospace headquarters and nuclear submarine reactor facilities in Derby. It sits within proximity to East Midlands Airport and the UK’s only inland Freeport.

3.15 The 360 acre mixed-use development will deliver:

4,530 new homes

3.45 million square feet of mixed employment space creating around 5,000 jobs

2 local centres and community facilities including new schools

transport infrastructure including completion of A50 Junction and Link Road (part-funded through £50 million Levelling Up Fund)

3.16 EMCCA and Homes England are working with partners to provide strategic leadership and refreshed programme governance. The JDU will continue to provide coordinated, cross-partner interventions to accelerate delivery of IGV.

Strategic place priority 2: Canal Corridor

3.17 The Canal Corridor Growth Zone focuses on Chesterfield, with strong links into South Yorkshire and Lincolnshire. There are significant opportunities for investment including around advanced manufacturing and the low carbon economy, as well as housing growth, with potential to deliver:

3,900 new homes

7,800 new jobs

£473 million in Gross Value Added (GVA) per year

Town Centre East, Chesterfield

3.18 Within the Canal Corridor, the JDU will initially focus on progressing opportunities in Chesterfield Town Centre, where there is potential for new homes at Spire Neighbourhood, Waterside, and the Station Quarter. The JDU will work with Chesterfield Borough Council to explore acceleration, funding options, and delivery models.

Strategic Place Priority 3: Peaks and Dales

3.19 The rural communities in the west of the region also need housing for local people, delivered in a way that addresses affordability issues related to second homes and holiday lets, as well as protection policies for sensitive sites and locations. Improved transport and digital infrastructure will assist these locations in diversifying their economies, attracting new businesses that can work remotely and stimulating local economies on a more sustained, less seasonal, basis.

Buxton

3.20 Within the Peaks and Dales Growth zone, the JDU will initially focus on Buxton. The opportunity for transformational change in Buxton seeks to bring new activity into the town centre. The JDU will work with High Peak Borough Council to explore the delivery strategy for this area.

4. Theme B: Housing and Regeneration Pipeline

4.1 Alongside the Growth Zones and priority schemes mentioned, EMCCA and Homes England will maintain, enhance and develop the Regional Housing Pipeline. This will enable delivery across the whole EMCCA area, including the Supercluster and Heartlands Growth Zones.

4.2 This will include:

investment-ready opportunities that are deliverable in the near-term

projects where co-development or the targeted application of expertise or enabling investment will unlock delivery

strategic growth and regeneration opportunities where a more integrated approach is required to unlock transformational change

4.3 Through the partnership, both organisations will work together to identify and focus activity where aligned land, investment, delivery powers and expertise, or market engagement can have the greatest impact in unlocking delivery.

4.4 Through the JDU, working with wider public sector partners, the partners will identify a portfolio of priority sites, explore barriers to delivery, and identify potential for longer-term and replicable approaches that could accelerate housing delivery, regeneration and economic growth.

4.5 Early work will include:

maximising the impact of the EMCCA Brownfield Housing Fund to support regeneration and affordable housing provision

optimising the impact of joint investment opportunities

establishing the Affordable Housing Working Group (AHWG)

a joined-up approach to engagement with Local Authorities, Registered Providers, and the wider sector to enhance the quality and understanding of the regional pipeline

5. Theme C: Shared thematic priorities

5.1 Achieving the scale of change envisaged through the Growth Plan requires more than investment. It requires greater alignment between local priorities, national capability, and investment decision-making.

5.2 The thematic priorities set out here focus on areas where greater local influence, coordinated action, and aligned investment can have the greatest impact on housing delivery, regeneration outcomes, and economic growth. They will help create the conditions required to unlock a stronger pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities and support the region’s long-term ambitions.

Social and affordable housing and council housebuilding delivery

5.3 Delivery of social and affordable housing is one of the clearest examples of how this PDA will bring decision-making, delivery capability and accountability closer to place.

5.4 Through this Agreement, the JDU will ensure social and affordable housing investment is aligned with the Mayor’s priorities for growth, regeneration and housing delivery. By combining regional decision-making with dedicated delivery capability and specialist affordable housing expertise, the partnership will enable investment decisions to be shaped more directly by local priorities and delivery opportunities.

5.5 Establishing an AHWG as part of the JDU, partners will work together to maximise the impact of this investment, increase the pace and scale of delivery, and ensure affordable housing investment supports wider regeneration, economic growth and placemaking ambitions.

5.6 Through this partnership, the parties will seek to facilitate the delivery of the Mayor’s ambition for social and affordable homes across the Region between 2026 and 2036, including increasing the scale of council house delivery alongside broader regeneration and economic growth outcomes.

5.7 The partnership will maintain and enhance the EMCCA housing pipeline, ensuring activity and investment are directed towards opportunities that can unlock or accelerate delivery, address housing need and contribute to the ambitions of the Local Growth Plan.

5.8 This will include:

a) Working with Registered Provider Strategic Partners operating within the SAHP to align investment plans and develop a coordinated pipeline of social and affordable housing opportunities across the Region, supporting delivery of the Mayor’s affordable housing and regeneration priorities.

b) Establishing an Affordable Housing Working Group as part of the JDU to jointly oversee affordable housing activity across the region, supporting the Mayor’s affordable housing and regeneration priorities.

c) SAHP decisions on Continuous Market Engagement (CME) will be delegated to the Regional SAHP team (within agreed thresholds) with the JDU providing the governance forum for approval to enable investment decisions to be locally led.

d) EMCCA will be given full visibility of the affordable housing pipeline data in their area. Through the JDU and enhanced governance, they will be included in the affordable housing pipeline review and CME assessment process providing local insights and data to develop proposals.

e) EMCCA will be involved in the assessment and decision-making process for further procurement rounds or extensions to existing Strategic Partnership allocations that affect the region.

f) A clearly defined escalation process if members of the JDU cannot agree on the SAHP CME investment decision to be made, via the PDA and, or, JDU or respective governance structures for a definitive decision. This will be through monthly governance.

5.9 Recognising the government’s ambition to significantly increase council housebuilding, Homes England will support EMCCA to:

review the barriers to delivery of council housing and work collaboratively with local authorities to implement the preferred approaches including the potential to align with other thematic areas including land, industrialised construction and other forms of investment

bring empty homes back into use and make other improvements to existing stock including where there are positive links to be made to other policy areas such as reduced use of temporary accommodation

Place-based investment and finance

5.10 Delivery of the region’s housing and regeneration ambitions will require investment at a scale that cannot be achieved through grant funding alone. Unlocking transformational opportunities across the region will depend on the ability to combine public and private capital, recycle investment over time and develop investable propositions capable of attracting long-term institutional funding.

5.11 This next phase of devolution presents an opportunity to move beyond traditional grant funding towards a more integrated regional investment model. EMCCA, Homes England and the NHB commit to aligning investment, funding and delivery activity around shared regional priorities, supporting housing-led growth and enabling greater levels of private investment.

5.12 The NHB, launched by Homes England in 2026, has been established to accelerate the delivery of new homes and mixed-use regeneration schemes through flexible public investment. Backed by up to £16 billion of debt, equity and guarantee products, the Bank is designed to work with national, regional and local partners to unlock housing delivery, crowd-in private capital and support the government’s ambition to deliver 1.5 million homes.

5.13 EMCCA, Homes England and the NHB share an ambition to use the PDA as a platform to develop innovative approaches to place-based investment, enhancing the existing regional housing pipeline of investable opportunities and increasing the scale of private capital investment into the region.

5.14 As part of this Agreement, the NHB will actively seek opportunities to amplify the region’s local investment fund supporting housing and regeneration ambitions and the Mayor’s priorities to attract wider investment using its lending, equity or guarantee capacity. The first phase of this work will focus on the development of a shared investment framework, operating principles and investment criteria, aligned to the mandate of the NHB and the strategic priorities of EMCCA.

5.15 The NHB will support the development of a portfolio of investment opportunities capable of unlocking a significantly greater level of private and institutional capital investment over time. Partners will work together to identify and develop housing-led regeneration, infrastructure-enabled growth, mixed-use development and strategic land opportunities that have the potential to unlock significantly greater levels of private and institutional investment over time.

5.16 The partnership will seek to:

maintain and enhance the prioritised pipeline of investable housing and regeneration opportunities across the EMCCA area

align NHB products and investment capabilities with Mayoral growth and regeneration priorities

crowd-in institutional and private-sector capital alongside public investment

establish the right frameworks to maximise the new opportunities to align investment around place priorities

explore innovative approaches to land, infrastructure and development finance that accelerate delivery and improve viability

develop replicable investment models that can be applied across a wider pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities

5.17 By combining devolved funding, NHB investment and private capital, EMCCA will test a new model of place-based investment providing a flexible source of capital designed to accelerate delivery, improve viability and support long-term economic growth.

Construction skills

5.18 To achieve EMCCA’s growth ambitions, there is a need to address ongoing skills shortages and gaps within the construction sector. To cover this, EMCCA has established the Construction Skills Package (CSP) to respond to this. The CSP has 3 core objectives:

Increasing course supply.

Increasing quality and capacity.

Strengthen links between learners, providers and employers.

5.19 Examples of the CSP in action are EMCCA funding of £1.3 million into construction-related skills bootcamps and free courses for jobs, £3 million capital funding into Construction Technical Excellence College to expand capacity for learners over 16 in further education colleges, sixth form colleges and 16-to-19 academies and a look to establish industry placements in the future.

5.20 A vibrant housing market plays an important role in employment and training opportunities, and creating the conditions for investment and development activity via the PDA will support the local ambition to realise those opportunities, and the JDU will explore opportunities to secure construction skills and employment related social value outputs from key projects.

6. Framework for delivery, governance, and implementation

6.1 To take this agreement forward EMCCA, Homes England, and the NHB commit to progressing a Joint Delivery Plan outlining key tasks, milestones and resourcing commitments, underpinned by a governance framework which delivers on the principles outlined in this PDA.

6.2 This will help to strengthen local capability to support delivery, while recognising a desire to go further in boosting the capacity, expertise and sharing of good practice across the public and private sector partners in the sub-region via a focused programme of activity.

6.3 As an Established Mayoral Strategic Authority, EMCCA is increasingly able to provide strategic leadership across the region, convening Homes England, local authorities, registered providers, government departments and other partners around shared priorities. Successful delivery will require ongoing collaboration between all relevant delivery partners. The PDA provides a framework through which EMCCA’s convening role can be translated into coordinated action to align partners, overcome system barriers, and coordinate activity around shared objectives.

Partnership commitments

6.4 The parties commit to:

align resources around agreed priorities

maintain and develop a shared Regional Housing Pipeline of development and investment opportunities

jointly identify and resolve barriers

convene stakeholders and align activity

share intelligence and investment planning

support delivery through a dedicated JDU

6.5 This PDA will operate on a 3-year basis and will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains aligned with evolving national policy, Mayoral priorities, market conditions and delivery opportunities. Delivery of the PDA will be supported through:

a rolling delivery programme maintained through the JDU, responding to Mayoral priorities, interventions and opportunities requiring joint action

a detailed annual Delivery Plan, agreed following approval of the PDA, translating strategic priorities into specific actions, responsibilities, milestones and resource commitments

an annual review process to refresh delivery priorities, resource allocations and pipeline activity without requiring the full PDA to be renegotiated

regular monitoring and performance reporting through the governance and accountability arrangements within this PDA, enabling partners to track progress, identify emerging risks and agree corrective action where required

6.6 The parties acknowledge that successful delivery will require ongoing collaboration between Homes England, the NHB, EMCCA and wider delivery partners including local authorities, government departments, infrastructure providers, registered providers, investors and other stakeholders.

Joint Delivery Unit

6.7 The JDU will provide a single delivery interface between EMCCA, Homes England, and the NHB to drive implementation of agreed priorities through the following functions:

programme management

pipeline development

opportunity identification

investment coordination

risk management

performance monitoring

6.8 Provisional capacity and capability estimates have been used in formulating this agreement. These will be refined and confirmed in the follow-on Delivery Plan for both Homes England and EMCCA. Indicative Homes England resources by capability are set out here.

Homes England resourcing of the JDU

Oversight, accountability and place leadership

Senior leadership and accountability, Executive Regional Director (ERD) — Leadership and sponsorship of Place Delivery Agreements within Homes England. Provides the strategic interface between local leaders and the Agency, aligning national priorities with local ambitions, resolving barriers to delivery, and ensuring places can rapidly access the full breadth of agency capabilities.

Partnership management and place co-ordination

Partnership management and coordination (including diagnostics and skills commissioning). Day-to-day partnership leadership. Develops strategic priorities with EMCCA; coordinates development and delivery of associated delivery plans and pipelines; undertakes diagnostics; facilitates relationship brokerage between public and private sector partners (including different parts of government); and leads relevant workstreams as required.

Delivery support — Day-to-day working level support for the above activities.

Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) interface — Responsible for coordinating affordable housing investment via SAHP in the EMCCA area.

National Housing Bank interface — Responsible for coordinating NHB activity in the EMCCA area.

Pipeline and Business Development

Pipeline Development — Provide cross-disciplinary expertise across both HE and the NHB, working closely with partnership leadership to identify, develop and progress pipeline projects. This includes applying technical expertise to identify opportunities, diagnose delivery challenges, engage and work collaboratively with partners and delivery bodies, and develop robust investment propositions across a range of funding and investment products, including those operated by EMCCA.

Project delivery

Project Delivery — Overall leadership and project-level support through the end-to-end development process, deploying expertise across strategic priorities and leveraging the full range of investment tools, interventions and products available to HE, the NHB and EMCCA.

Land assembly, planning, enabling and disposal — Expertise related to strategically acquiring land, preparing it for development through de-risking and pre development interventions, and disposing of and managing delivery through partners, including through a master development approach.

Infrastructure planning, provision, and contract management — Expertise related to the financing, delivery and management of complex infrastructure projects.

Project funding and investment — Expertise related to identifying and structuring project funding requirements, and identifying suitable sources of funding and investment from Homes England, the NHB, EMCCA and, or, other public and private sources.

Affordable housing delivery — Expertise related to structuring/securing affordable housing provision aligned to local priorities — including through managing relationships with local affordable housing providers.

Shared thematic capability

6.9 The JDU will be complemented by housing delivery expertise from across the wider agency shaped to develop products, schemes and initiatives as part of this thematic capability, including on:

social and affordable housing

NHB finance and product specialists

specialist technical capabilities

strategy, research and innovation capacity

Specialist capabilities

6.10 In the first instance, the specialist capabilities that the JDU has access to are expected to comprise the following:

Advisory Team Large Application Sites (ATLAS) (specialist planning support)

New Homes Accelerator

Climate, Environment and Sustainability

Design, Masterplanning and Placemaking

Community Engagement and Social Impact

Strategic Planning

Compulsory Purchase Order

Estate Management and Contingent Assets and Liabilities

Capital Projects Delivery

Research and Analysis including market engagement

Economics

Geospatial

Commercial and Procurement Strategy

Risk Management

SME and Complex Development Loans (National Housing Bank)

Equity and Joint Venture Partnerships (National Housing Bank)

Guarantees (National Housing Bank)

Infrastructure Loans (National Housing Bank)

Low Interest Loans (National Housing Bank)

Governance and accountability

6.11 The Governance Framework will be developed further through the Delivery Plan and will include:

creating significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor

establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the chairs of Homes England and the NHB, and the chief executives of both organisations

introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes

6.12 In recognition of the commitment to create an even more responsive and re-wired delivery body as outlined in the Housing Minister’s letter, and to bring decision-making and accountability closer to impacted communities, the parties will commit in parallel to review existing delegations, reporting and accountability frameworks. Communications and stakeholder engagement activity will similarly be reviewed within the same timeframe to maximise Homes England’s impact. Homes England will ensure information on planned activity within the EMCCA area is shared in advance via the JDU.

Delivery Plan

6.13 The PDA will be supported by a detailed Delivery Plan which will provide the primary mechanism for coordinating delivery activity and monitoring progress against agreed commitments.

6.14 The Delivery Plan will:

translate the strategic priorities and commitments set out within this PDA into deliverable programmes, projects and interventions

identify, for each commitment or activity, the responsible organisation or organisations, lead owner, milestones, review dates, expected outputs and outcomes, and success measures

set out funding requirements, resource commitments, critical dependencies, reporting arrangements, risks and mitigation measures

maintain a forward pipeline of opportunities and activities to support delivery of shared priorities

identify areas where additional collaboration, investment or intervention may be required to achieve agreed outcomes

6.15 Following approval of the PDA, the partners will jointly prepare the initial Delivery Plan.

6.16 The partners will agree:

the timetable for preparation and implementation of the Delivery Plan

the lead organisation responsible for coordinating drafting and updates

governance arrangements for review, endorsement and approval

the senior officers authorised to approve revisions and updates

reporting arrangements to support effective oversight and accountability

6.17 The JDU will coordinate preparation of the Delivery Plan, its annual review, and ensure that it remains a live document throughout the life of the PDA.

Annual review

6.18 The PDA will be subject to an annual review led by the JDU and overseen through the governance arrangements referred to in this PDA. It will report to the Mayor and the Chief Executive and Chair of Homes England.

6.19 The review will:

assess progress against the commitments and success measures set out in the Delivery Plan

consider emerging opportunities, risks and policy developments

review resource requirements and delivery capacity

refresh the rolling programme of activity and priority projects

recommend amendments to the Delivery Plan where required

6.20 Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, changes arising through the annual review process will be managed through updates to the Delivery Plan and will not require the PDA itself to be redrafted or re-executed.

6.21 This approach will ensure that the PDA remains a stable long-term framework while enabling partners to adapt delivery activity in response to changing circumstances and opportunities.

1. Confidentiality

1.1 In this clause the following words and expressions have the following meaning:

Confidential Information means the terms of this PDA and all information whether oral or written (on whatever medium stored) relating to this PDA disclosed or made available, directly or indirectly by one party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers to the other party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers but excludes any information which:

(i) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, publicly available;

(ii) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, available to the Recipient from a person who, to the Recipient’s knowledge, is not under any confidential obligation in respect of that information; or

(iii) has been independently acquired by a Party without breaching any of their respective obligations in this PDA.

1.2 Each Party recognises that under this PDA it may receive Confidential Information belonging to the other.

1.3 Each Party agrees to treat all Confidential Information belonging to the other as confidential and not to disclose such Confidential Information or any other confidential information relating to each other arising or coming to its attention in the course of this PDA to any third party without the prior written consent of the other Party and agrees not to use such Confidential Information for any purpose other than that for which it is supplied under this PDA.

1.4 The obligations of confidence referred to in Clause 1.3 shall not apply to any Confidential Information which:

(a) is in, or which comes into, the public domain otherwise than by reason of a breach of this PDA or of any other duty of confidentiality relating to that information; or

(b) is obtained from a third party without that third party being under an obligation (express or implied) to keep the information confidential; or

(c) is lawfully in the possession of the other Party before the date of this PDA and in respect of which that Party is not under an existing obligation of confidentiality; or

(d) is independently developed without access to the Confidential Information of the other Party.

1.5 Each Party will be permitted to disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to do so:

(a) to enable the disclosing party to perform its obligations under this PDA; or by any applicable law or by a court, arbitral or administrative tribunal in the course of proceedings before it including without limitation any requirement for disclosure under Freedom of Information Laws (as defined in clause 2) and the Parties acknowledge that any lists or schedules provided by it outlining Confidential Information are of indicative value only and that the other party may nevertheless be obliged to disclose such confidential information; or

(b) by any regulatory body (including any investment exchange) acting in the course of proceedings before it or acting in the course of its duties; or

(c) in order to give proper instructions to any professional adviser of that Party who also has an obligation to keep any such Confidential Information confidential.

1.6 The Parties shall ensure that all Confidential Information obtained from the other Party under or in connection with this PDA:-

(a) is given only to such of its employees, professional advisors or consultants engaged to advise it in connection with this PDA as is strictly necessary for the performance of this PDA and only to the extent necessary for the performance of this PDA;

(b) is treated as confidential and not disclosed (without Homes England’s prior written approval) or used by any such staff or professional advisors or consultants otherwise than for the purposes of this PDA and in all instances such third parties are subject to a signed confidentiality undertaking.

1.7 Notwithstanding any other provision of this PDA, nothing in this agreement shall prevent Homes England:

(a) disclosing any Confidential Information for the purpose of:

(i) the examination and certification of its accounts; or

(ii) any examination pursuant to section 6(1) of the National Audit Act 1983 of the economy, efficiency and effectiveness with which Homes England has used its resources; or

(b) disclosing any Confidential Information to any other department, office or agency of the Crown provided that in disclosing such Confidential Information pursuant to this paragraph (b), it discloses only the information which is necessary for the purpose concerned and requires that the information is treated in confidence.

Freedom of Information Laws means the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 and any subordinate legislation made thereunder from time to time together with any guidance and ,or, codes of practice issued by the Information Commissioner in relation to such legislation;

2.2 The Parties are each a public authority as defined under the Freedom of Information Laws and so may be required to disclose information in response to a request for information under those laws (Request for Information). (a) where appropriate and as soon as reasonably practicable inform the other Party that it has received a request to disclose information in response to a request for information under the Freedom of Information Laws; and

(b) in relation to such information and pursuant to the Freedom of Information Laws, consider the application of the exceptions and exemptions to disclosure before complying with any obligation to disclose such information.
